name: Hack

subjectOf.text: The DAO failed because of fundamental flaws in its own code, which allowed hackers to move one third of its funds to a subsidiary account, showing that governance built entirely on smart contracts inherits the defects of its code.
subjectOf.abstract: Alas, things went terribly wrong with the DAO. Fundamental flaws in the DAO code enabled hackers to transfer one third of the total funds to a subsidiary account.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Blockchain Innovation for Private Investment Funds (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2998033
scope_conditions: applies to organizations whose governance and asset control rest entirely on open source smart contract code

subjectOf.text: The DAO failed because its code had not yet been perfected: hackers took a third of the DAO tokens and transferred them to another account, and that hack together with other technological limitations led to the demise of the DAO.
subjectOf.abstract: Unfortunately, the code had not yet been perfected and hackers were able to take a third of the DAO tokens and transfer them into another account. This hack and other technological limitations, led to the demise of the DAO.58
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Blockchain Technology and Race in Corporate America (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3071378
scope_conditions: The DAO, launched May 2016 on Ethereum

subjectOf.text: Fundamental flaws in the DAO code enabled hackers to transfer one third of total funds to a subsidiary account, and that hack combined with additional technological limitations brought down the first DAO initiative.
subjectOf.abstract: This hack in combination with additional technological limitations brought down the first DAO initiative.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Blockchain Solutions for Agency Problems in Corporate Governance (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3373393
